slots.hypothesis: The alpha source is the nominal price level itself. It is the only necessary part shared by 4 heads: knocking out the cs_first_low20 screen costs +1.81 and +3.43, and the screened y alone is negative. Open/Close, pow_3 and ts_decay_linear do not matter. It survives the linear LogFloatCap control only because of the tail-indicator nonlinearity. The 14 seeds replace the one periphery seen so far (cs_first_low20(y, price) plus 1e-7 decorations) with: double sorts (price inside size, total-cap, liquidity and ListAge deciles); the price residual after regressing on cubed size (Barra non-linear size); excluding the cheapest 5% or 10%; price relative to its own 120d high and 60d z-score; price-tier-relative return and skew (Green-Hwang, Birru-Wang); and float-expansion-vs-price-fall inside the cheap segment (Pontiff-Woodgate). The family control is the 4 heads that contain the core.

Intraday volume timing is cross-sectional information off the price/size axis: stocks whose volume is concentrated early do better. It comes from the main term of head +0.58, -2*day_centroid(sqrt(Volume)), with enrichment n=9 and +0.64. The 14 seeds split it the ways the literature does: morning-session volume share (in_half), where the heaviest 10% of minutes fall, the return sign of the heaviest minutes (stealth trading), the timing shift against the stock's own 20d habit, volume timing vs |ret| timing, the centroid within size deciles, and persistence of the morning return. The raw centroid goes to R because it may hit the rho>=0.7 library ban against head +0.58.
